CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with a significant past medical history of type I diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux, who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports associated lower extremity swelling and lethargy, which he attributes to dietary indiscretion from attending house parties and consuming salty foods. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with exertion such as walking up stairs. Patient denies dyspnea at rest currently but reports one episode of acute dyspnea at night approximately one week ago that has not recurred. Patient also reports morning stiffness, discomfort lying flat in bed, and initial difficulty with ambulation upon waking.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for shortness of breath and lower extremity edema. Denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type I diabetes mellitus on insulin pump
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Gastroesophageal reflux disease

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports affinity for chocolate bars. During working weeks, he monitors blood sugars closely but admits to poor monitoring on weekends due to being busy. Has attempted natural solutions for depression including outdoor stretching in summer months but notes difficulty maintaining this with weather changes. Not currently on psychiatric medications but open to suggestions. Has been making lifestyle modifications for reflux including reducing Red Bull, caffeine, and alcohol intake, noting difficulty with alcohol reduction during holidays but improved compliance.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs stable with satisfactory oxygenation levels. Neck exam: no jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits. Cardiac exam: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Pulmonary exam: bilateral crackles appreciated at the bases. Lower extremity exam: 1+ pitting edema noted.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease
Labs: White blood cell count not elevated, no evidence of pneumonia

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Initiate Lasix 40 mg daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and call if weight does not decrease or if weight increases. Patient instructed to call or seek emergency care with 911 if dyspnea worsens at rest, as may require intravenous diuretics.
2. Type I diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess need for adjustments. Follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam completed.
3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications initiated at this time.
4. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.
